track: CDCETH/CDCBTC deployed-token role and auxiliary rate-limit reachability review

scopeBasis.validationMode: Local source analysis plus read-only eth_call/event/source queries; no transactions were sent.

localFoundryPoC.proofScope: Self-contained exact-logic harness for the RateLimit source; does not by itself prove an attacker can reach a deployed production forwarder or raise severity.

observations: Expected strict-equality detector on the already-known RateLimit full-quota early return.
Unused-return and reentrancy-events detector hits are not independently exploitable findings here: calls are to the configured token path and no untrusted callback path/asset impact was established.

A complete Slither compile of LiquidETHV1/Centre dependencies did not complete because this sandbox's partially installed legacy npm dependency graph and old-solc source path mapping were incompatible; no claim of successful whole-project analysis is made.

productionStateReadOnly.interpretation: These observations confirm privileged token minter configuration, not an attacker-controlled route. The known RateLimit 2x PoC applies only if a caller is configured on a deployed MintForwarder/ExchangeRateUpdater that itself has production mint/oracle authority. That production link was not found in the official repo's current mainnet manifests; Ethereum CDCETH's single public MinterConfigured event points to its owner/master-minter EOA, not a forwarder. Cronos historical log coverage was limited by public-node range/API-key restrictions, so absence of Cronos forwarder configuration is not claimed as fully proven.

impactAndDisposition.reason: Code-level rate-limit bypass is reproducible in an isolated harness, but no public attacker path or production deployed forwarder/token-role connection is proven. The affected mint/update callers are allowlisted by owner; no unauthorized mint, rate manipulation, or real funds impact was performed or observed.

doNotRepeat: Do not rerun the exact local 2x RateLimit harness as evidence of production exploitability; it only tests contract logic in isolation.
Do not infer a live forwarder from source presence or from a direct owner's minter allowance.
Do not transmit any transaction to the production token, oracle, or minter contracts.
Do not elevate the existing CDC-SC-01 above its documented High/Medium candidate status absent a proven deployed configuration and realistic attacker path.
nextHypothesis: Pivot to another Critical-eligible public surface or a new on-chain integration graph: resolve the actual configured roles/consumer contracts from verified deployment artifacts and passive chain data, then test only a source-supported unauthenticated transition in a local fork. Do not enumerate/mutate production roles or submit requests/signatures.
